plan: This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: bidding higher risks paying more than your value if you win against a bid between your value and your bid, while bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Since I have no information suggesting otherwise (first round, no history), I will bid exactly my value of $30 to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value. This ensures that if I win, I pay less than my value (profit), and if my value is lower than others, I simply lose without any loss. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $7, I will bid $7.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, the dominant strategy is to bid exactly my true value, regardless of what others bid. This is because if I win, I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid), so bidding my true value ensures I never overpay and always capture positive profit when I have the highest valuation. Bidding above value risks negative profit; bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior round history to suggest otherwise, I'll bid my true value of $36.
